Begin the adventure "The Lost Mine of Whisperhollow". My character is Bramble Thornfoot. Refer to the CLAUDE.md for DM instructions. Set the scene and begin the story.
Let me pull up the scenario details and character sheets to get us started properly.

I notice Pip is at 7/10 HP — I'll accept that as-is per the rules (no session-start equalization). Now let me set the scene!

---

# 🏔️ The Lost Mine of Whisperhollow
### *What Was Sealed Below Was Never Meant to Be Forgotten*

---

The crumpled letter sits heavy in your pocket, Bramble — stained with road dust and the faint impression of desperate fingers. An old dwarven woman named Brenna Stonemantle, village elder of a place called Whisperhollow, begging for help. *Strange sounds from the mine. Livestock spooked. Three villagers missing.*

And, of course, the promise of coin. Meager coin, but coin nonetheless. 💰

Your ragtag band of companions has been on the road for two days now, climbing a narrow mountain trail that switchbacks through pine forest and loose scree. The air is getting thinner. The conversation, somehow, is not.

---

**"—and THAT,"** Eldon Fairweather says, adjusting his brass goggles for the fourteenth time in the last hour, **"is why the tensile properties of starsteel are theoretically superior to adamantine, assuming you account for the harmonic resonance of the crystalline lattice, which most smiths DON'T, because — oh, is that a hawk circling? Fascinating wing geometry. Anyway, most smiths are frankly —"**

Drak grunts. That's it. Just a grunt. But somehow it conveys an entire paragraph of *"Please stop talking."* Talon, perched on his shoulder, ruffles his feathers in what might be agreement. 🦅

**"Don't mind him, friend,"** Pip chimes in from behind you, his cheerful voice cutting through the mountain air like warm butter through bread — which, coincidentally, is exactly what he's doing, slicing a loaf he somehow produced from his pack. **"Here, Eldon, have a bite. My gran always said a full mouth is a quiet mouth — ah, she meant it lovingly, of course."** 🍞

Vaelith brings up the rear, her plum velvet cloak somehow immaculate despite two days of trail dust. **"Darling,"** she drawls to no one in particular, **"when the letter said 'declining village,' I assumed it meant the property values, not the road quality."** She steps delicately over a rock. **"If this Brenna Stonemantle turns out to be a goat farmer with an overactive imagination, someone owes me new boots."** 👠

Sister Mirael walks in silence at the edge of the trail, one hand trailing along the treeline. She pauses, amber eyes scanning the valley ahead.

**"...The trees are listening,"** she says quietly. **"They have been for the last mile."** 🌲

And then the valley opens before you.

---

> *The road narrows as you climb into the valley, the mountains pressing close on either side like the walls of a corridor. Whisperhollow reveals itself gradually — first a crumbling stone wall, then scattered cottages with dark windows, and finally a modest village square dominated by an ancient well. The only sign of life is a weathered tavern called the Pickaxe & Pint, its swinging sign creaking in the mountain breeze. From somewhere deep in the earth beneath your feet, you feel more than hear a low, rhythmic vibration, like the heartbeat of the mountain itself.* ⛏️🍺

---

The sun is sinking behind the western peaks, painting the sky in bruised purples and golds. A thin curl of chimney smoke rises from the tavern. The village looks... tired. Worn down. Like it's been holding its breath for forty years and is about ready to exhale for the last time. 😔

Drak's hand drifts to his longbow. **"Quiet,"** he mutters. **"Too quiet."** Talon launches from his shoulder and spirals upward, scanning.

**"Oh, how original,"** Vaelith murmurs. **"'Too quiet.' Someone alert the bards."** ✨

But even she's not smiling.

---

**Bramble** — you're standing at the edge of Whisperhollow as evening falls. The tavern glows ahead. The village square and its ancient well are to your left. And up the hillside to the north, you can just make out a dark shape set into the mountainside — the sealed mine entrance. 🏔️

Your criminal instincts are already working. What do you do first?

**Some options (but you're not limited to these):**
- 🍺 Head to the **Pickaxe & Pint** to gather rumors and get the lay of the land
- 🗣️ Seek out **Brenna Stonemantle** directly to hear her plea
- 👀 **Scout the village** first — note the exits, the valuables, the vibe
- ⛏️ Head straight for the **mine entrance** to have a look before dark
Let's go into the tavern. I will burst in with song about saving the town. Am I a falsetto or soprano?

A halfling rogue with a flair for the dramatic? Love it. 😂

You're a **tenor** — surprisingly clear and carrying for someone three feet tall, with a slightly raspy edge from too many smoky tavern nights. Think "charming street performer" more than "choir boy." But honestly, what matters more is the *confidence*, and Bramble Thornfoot has that in spades. 🎶

Let's see how this lands with the locals. Given you're making a grand entrance to impress strangers, I'd say this calls for a **Performance check** — which for you is a straight Charisma check (no proficiency in Performance).

Let's hear it! 🎲
Performance check — 1d20+2: 20 + 2 = 22

### 🎵 NATURAL 20! Total: 22 🎵

Oh, Bramble. You *magnificent* little showman.

---

You kick open the door of the Pickaxe & Pint with one booted foot — which, given your height, mostly just shoves it open at knee level, but the *energy* is immaculate — and belt out in a ringing tenor that fills every dusty corner of the room:

> 🎶 *"Fear not, good folk of Whisperhollow town!*
> *Your mountain shakes but we won't let you down!*
> *Six blades, six hearts, one hawk upon the wing—*
> *We've come to slay your darkness, so tonight we DRINK and SING!"* 🎶

The tavern goes dead silent.

A dozen weathered faces stare at you from behind half-empty mugs. A dog under a table lifts its head. A log pops in the fireplace. 🪵

Then an old shepherd in the corner starts *clapping*. 👏

And like a dam breaking, the whole room erupts. Mugs slam on tables. Someone actually *cheers*. A tired-looking woman behind the bar — stout, flour-dusted, clearly the owner — cracks the first smile she's worn in weeks and starts pulling ales. 🍺

**"Well now,"** Pip says from behind you, beaming like a proud parent. **"That's how you make an entrance, friends. Bramble, my gran would've loved you."** 🥲

Vaelith slow-claps from the doorway. **"I'll admit it, darling. I'm... almost impressed."** She pauses. **"Don't let it go to your head. It's already disproportionately large for your body."** 😏

Drak steps inside, scans the room with practiced eyes, grunts once — but the corner of his mouth twitches. Just for a second. 

Eldon is already distracted. **"Fascinating acoustic properties in here — low ceiling, stone walls, the resonance is — oh! Is that a *map* behind the bar?"** 🗺️

Sister Mirael enters last, quiet as a shadow, and takes a position near the wall where she can see the whole room. She gives you the smallest nod. From her, that's a standing ovation. 🌿

---

The barkeep sets a foaming mug in front of you with a thunk. **"On the house, little master. We haven't had a reason to smile in weeks."** She leans in, lowering her voice. **"You're the ones answering Brenna's letter, aren't you? Thank the gods. She'll want to see you — she's just up the lane at the shrine. But warm yourselves first. You'll need it for what's ahead."**

From the corner, a grizzled old man with a wild gray beard and rheumy eyes glares at you from behind his mug. 👴

**"Fools,"** he mutters, loud enough for everyone to hear. **"Singing about slaying darkness. That mine'll swallow you whole, same as it swallowed the others. Mark old Tormund's words."**

The room's warmth cools just a fraction.

---

The tavern is yours, Bramble. You've got the crowd on your side — for now. What's the play? 🎭

- 🍻 **Work the room** — buy a round, loosen some tongues, gather rumors
- 👴 **Confront old Tormund** — what does he know about the mine?
- 🗺️ **Check out that map** behind the bar that caught Eldon's eye
- 🚪 **Head to the shrine** to meet Brenna Stonemantle
- Something else entirely?
Let's work the room

Time to do what Bramble does best — be everybody's best friend while quietly cataloguing everything worth knowing (and everything worth *nicking*). 😏

You've already won the room with that entrance, so let's see how well you press the advantage. This is a **Persuasion check** — you're proficient in Deception, not Persuasion, but your natural Charisma still carries weight. And honestly, with that Nat 20 performance still buzzing in the air, I'll give you **advantage** on this check. The crowd *wants* to talk to you.
Persuasion (adv) — 2d20+2: [3, 18] + 2 = 23

With advantage, we take the higher: **18 + 2 = 20.** Against a DC 12 to get the villagers talking freely — that's a handsome success. ✅

Meanwhile, let's see if your keen rogue eyes pick up anything the others might miss. **Perception check** (you're proficient):
Perception check — 1d20+2: 6 + 2 = 8

Perception: **6 + 2 = 8** against DC 12. Hmm. Not your sharpest evening — maybe it's the free ale. 🍺

Let's also see what Eldon makes of that map behind the bar — **History check** (he's proficient, +5):
Eldon History — 1d20+5: 4 + 5 = 9

Eldon History: **4 + 5 = 9** against DC 14. The gnome's too excited to focus. 📜

---

You grab your free ale, flash the barkeep your best crooked grin, and get to *work*.

Within twenty minutes, you've made a full circuit of the Pickaxe & Pint. A coin here, a toast there, a well-timed joke about a goat — the standard Bramble Thornfoot playbook. 🐐💰 Here's what you piece together:

### 🗣️ What the Villagers Know (or Think They Know):

- **The mine's been sealed for forty years.** Old iron doors, welded shut by the dwarves who used to run the place. Nobody alive remembers exactly *why* — just that it happened fast, and the dwarves left shortly after.

- **The noises started about three weeks ago.** A deep rhythmic *humming* from underground, felt more than heard. Gets worse at night. Rattles the windows. The sheep won't go near the hillside anymore. 🐑

- **Three villagers went to investigate two weeks ago** — a man named **Haldor**, a woman named **Miri**, and young **Tam**, a twelve-year-old boy. Tam is the younger brother of **Elara Windmere**, a shepherd who's been loudly demanding a rescue mission ever since. None of them have come back.

- **Nobody agrees on why the mine was sealed.** Some say a tunnel collapse killed dozens. Others whisper about cursed gold. One old woman insists the dwarves found "something that weren't meant to be found." 👀

- A few folks mention seeing **pale blue-white light** flickering behind the sealed mine doors at night. Most pretend they haven't seen it.

---

Meanwhile, Eldon has wedged himself behind the bar and is squinting at a faded, yellowed map pinned to the wall — an old diagram of the Ironvein Mine's upper tunnels. **"Fascinating, fascinating — standard dwarven radial design, spoke-and-hub layout with — hmm, the ink's faded terribly. I can make out the main shaft and maybe two or three branches, but anything past the first junction is just... smudges."** He frowns, tapping his chin. **"Still, better than nothing."** 🗺️

Drak has stationed himself by the window, ale untouched, watching the darkening hillside. Talon is perched on the windowsill. **"Light,"** Drak says quietly. **"Up at the mine. Flickering."**

Sister Mirael sits in a dim corner, nursing a cup of water. A stray cat has materialized in her lap and she's absently scratching its ears. She catches your eye and tilts her head toward old Tormund, who's been glowering at your group from his corner the whole time, muttering into his beard. 🐱

Pip, naturally, has found the kitchen. You can hear him back there cheerfully negotiating with the cook. **"No, no, friend — you want to add the rosemary BEFORE the stock reduces, trust me on this one —"** 🧑‍🍳

Vaelith has somehow acquired a second glass of wine and is engaged in a hushed conversation with a nervous-looking young woman at a side table — **Elara Windmere**, you realize. The shepherd. The missing boy's sister. Vaelith's expression is unusually... soft. She catches you looking and immediately rearranges her face into its usual mask of bored amusement. 🍷

---

The tavern is warm. The ale is decent. But outside, the last light is fading, and through the floorboards, you can feel that low, rhythmic pulse from deep underground. Like the mountain's heartbeat. Or its warning. 💓⛰️

**What's next, Bramble?**

- 👴 **Corner old Tormund** — Mirael's look suggested he's worth pressing
- 🐑 **Talk to Elara** — she knows the mountain paths and her brother is down there
- 🗺️ **Study the map** more closely with Eldon
- 🚪 **Head to the shrine** to see Brenna Stonemantle before it gets too late
- 🔍 Something else?
I run outside yelling, into the mine!

The ale sloshes as you slam your mug down, vault off the barstool, and bolt for the door.

**"INTO THE MINE, FRIENDS! NO TIME LIKE THE PRESENT!"** you holler over your shoulder, kicking the tavern door open into the cold mountain night. 🏃‍♂️💨

Behind you, chaos.

**"Wait — what? WHAT?"** Eldon squawks, fumbling his goggles back down. **"I haven't finished cataloguing the map's — oh, bother —"** He grabs his staff and scrambles after you.

Vaelith sets down her wine glass with the precise, controlled motion of someone suppressing a scream. **"Of course. Of course he's running into the haunted mine. At** ***night.***" She stands, adjusts her cloak, and follows. **"If I die, I'm haunting every single one of you."** 👻

Pip emerges from the kitchen with a half-wrapped bundle of bread. **"Oh! Are we — right now? Right, yes, okay!"** He tucks the bread into his pack mid-stride, and his cheerful expression sharpens into something focused. Ready. 🍞⚡

Drak is already outside. He was moving before you finished your sentence. Longbow in hand. Talon overhead. **"Reckless,"** he mutters. But he's not stopping you. He's *scouting ahead.* 🦅

Sister Mirael rises without a word, the cat spilling gracefully from her lap. She pauses at the door, her amber eyes finding yours in the dark.

**"...The moth does not ask the flame's permission,"** she says softly. Then she follows. 🌿

---

You charge up the hillside path, boots crunching on loose gravel, the cold night air burning in your lungs. The village falls away behind you. The stars are sharp and close overhead, and the twin moons cast the mountainside in pale silver light.

And there it is. ⛏️

> *The mine entrance looms before you, set into the mountainside like a wound in the rock. Two massive iron doors, green with age and webbed with cracks in their ancient welds, stand as the last barrier between the village and whatever stirs below. Dwarven runes circle the door frame in an unbroken ring, their edges still sharp despite decades of weathering. As you approach, the vibration in the ground intensifies, and the runes begin to glow with a faint blue-silver light, as if responding to your presence. Three bedrolls and a shattered lantern lie abandoned at the door's base — the missing villagers made it this far.* ✨🔮

The humming is much stronger here. You can feel it in your teeth. The runes pulse like a slow heartbeat — blue-silver, blue-silver — and a thin draft of warm, mineral-scented air seeps through the cracking welds.

Drak drops to a knee beside the abandoned bedrolls. **"Two weeks old. They camped here."** He examines the shattered lantern. **"Left in a hurry. No blood."** 🔍

Eldon is already at the door, face inches from the runes, practically vibrating with excitement. **"Oh — oh, this is *remarkable*. Pre-collapse dwarven wardcraft, a full protective circuit, and the resonance pattern suggests — yes, yes, this is a *rune lock.* Not a seal of destruction, a seal of *protection.* These doors aren't keeping something dangerous in. They're keeping something precious *safe.*"** 🧙‍♂️

The doors stand before you — massive, ancient, cracked but unbroken. The welds are failing, but they still hold.

---

**So, Bramble.** You're here. No turning back now. Getting through these doors is the first challenge. You've got a few options:

- 🧠 **Let Eldon try the rune lock** — he'll need an **Arcana check** (DC 13) to work out the sequence
- 💪 **Brute force it** — an **Athletics check** (DC 18) to wrench the failing welds apart. Loud. Very loud.
- 🔧 **Use your thieves' tools** on the welds/hinges — this is a dwarven lock, not a tumbler, but you might find a weakness
- 🔙 **Actually wait** — maybe talking to Brenna first would've been smart after all...

What's the play? ⚔️
Eldon and I shall have a go at it

Two big brains on one puzzle! Well — one big brain and one very nimble pair of hands. Let's see what you've got. 🧠🔧

Eldon goes first, pressing his face so close to the runes his nose nearly touches the stone. You crouch beside him, studying the mechanism from a more... *practical* angle.

**Eldon's Arcana check** (DC 13, +5):
Eldon Arcana — 1d20+5: 10 + 5 = 15

**Eldon Arcana: 10 + 5 = 15 vs DC 13 — Success!** ✅

And Bramble, you don't have Arcana proficiency, but you *do* have those expert thieves' tools and a knack for finding the mechanical weakness in things. Let's call this an **Investigation check** (you're proficient, +3) to see if you can assist Eldon from the practical side:
Bramble Investigation — 1d20+3: 19 + 3 = 22

**Bramble Investigation: 19 + 3 = 22!** Absolute *chef's kiss.* 🤌

---

Eldon's fingers dance across the rune ring, tracing patterns in the air. **"Yes, yes — it's a sequential ward. Moradin's hammer strikes — the classic dwarven cadence. First the anvil, then the spark, then the fold, then the quench. You trace the runes in the order of the forging process. Simple! Well, simple if you've read Thordak's** ***Treatise on Sacred Metalwork***, **which obviously I have, twice, though the second time was mostly for the footnotes which are frankly more interesting than the —"**

**"Eldon,"** you cut in, running your fingers along the door frame. **"There's a physical mechanism too. Feel this?"** 🔍

Your thieves' tools instincts have spotted what pure academia missed — behind the rune ring, there's a series of recessed stone pins, each one connected to a rune. It's not *just* magic. It's a mechanical lock *married* to an arcane one. The dwarves built in redundancy. Clever bastards.

**"Oh!"** Eldon's eyes go wide behind his goggles. **"Oh, that's BEAUTIFUL. A hybrid system! The runes provide the arcane authorization and the pins provide the physical release — you need BOTH. Bramble, you wonderful, larcenous little —"**

**"Less talking, more opening."** 😏

Together, you work in tandem. Eldon traces the runes in sequence — anvil, spark, fold, quench — and as each one flares blue-silver, you feel the corresponding pin *click* under your fingertips and ease it into position with your lockpicks.

One. Two. Three. **Four.**

---

A deep, resonant **THOOM** rolls through the mountain. The rune ring blazes brilliant blue-white for a single heartbeat, then fades to a gentle glow. The ancient welds *crack* — not violently, but deliberately, like a lock turning — and the massive iron doors groan inward on corroded hinges, releasing a long, slow exhalation of warm air that smells of stone and metal and something older than memory. 🌬️⛏️

The darkness beyond is absolute.

Then — a faint pulse of blue-silver light from deep, deep inside. And that humming, stronger now. Closer.

**"...Huh,"** Drak says from behind you, arrow nocked. **"Doors opened quiet. That's something."** 🏹

Vaelith peers over your heads into the black. **"Oh, splendid. A gaping maw of darkness. My absolute favourite."** She snaps her fingers and her golden eyes flare briefly — Darkvision at the ready. **"After you, gentlemen. I** ***insist.***" ✨

Pip has already lit a torch. Its warm light pushes back the first few feet of shadow, revealing a cramped antechamber beyond — overturned crates, rusted mining equipment, the collapsed remains of an old guard post.

And from behind those crates — a skittering sound. Claws on stone. 🐀

Drak's bowstring creaks taut. **"Company."**

---

Something is moving in the antechamber. Sounds like **two somethings**, low to the ground and fast. The scenario calls for **2 giant rats** nesting in the debris. 🐀🐀

**Bramble — do you want to:**
- ⚔️ **Rush in weapons drawn** — you've got a shortsword and the element of surprise
- 🏹 **Let Drak take the first shot** from the doorway while you sneak in
- 🔥 **Send Eldon's Fire Bolt in first** to light up the room and roast whatever's lurking
- 🤫 **Try to sneak in** — Stealth is your *specialty*, after all

Your call, boss! 🎯
In I go, screaming holding a dagger!

Classic Bramble! Subtlety is for *later*. 🗡️😤

A screaming halfling with a dagger charging into a dark room full of giant rats — let's roll initiative!
Bramble initiative — 1d20+3: 7 + 3 = 10
Drak initiative — 1d20+3: 10 + 3 = 13
Eldon initiative — 1d20+1: 13 + 1 = 14
Pip initiative — 1d20+3: 17 + 3 = 20
Mirael initiative — 1d20+2: 2 + 2 = 4
Vaelith initiative — 1d20+2: 3 + 2 = 5
Rat 1 initiative — 1d20+2: 19 + 2 = 21
Rat 2 initiative — 1d20+2: 9 + 2 = 11
Those rats are *quick*. Let me check their stats real fast.

Giant Rats from memory: AC 12, HP 7, +4 to hit, 1d4+2 piercing. Let's go! 🐀⚔️

---

## ⚔️ COMBAT — The Antechamber

**Initiative Order:**
1. 🐀 **Rat 1** — 21
2. 🥊 **Pip** — 20
3. 🧙 **Eldon** — 14
4. 🏹 **Drak** — 13
5. 🐀 **Rat 2** — 11
6. 🗡️ **Bramble** — 10
7. 👻 **Vaelith** — 5
8. 🌿 **Mirael** — 4

*The antechamber is cramped — about 15 feet across, cluttered with overturned crates and rusted equipment. Pip's torchlight spills in from the doorway behind you.*

---

### 🐀 Rat 1 — Turn 1

Your scream startles the rats out of hiding — but these aren't timid cellar mice. They're bloated, mange-covered beasts the size of hunting dogs, eyes gleaming red in the torchlight. The first one launches itself off a crate straight at the screaming halfling running toward it — that's you, Bramble! 😬
Rat 1 bite Bramble — 1d20+4: 11 + 4 = 15
**15 vs your AC 14 — that hits!** 🩸
Rat 1 damage — 1d4+2: 1 + 2 = 3

The rat sinks its yellow teeth into your forearm as you charge in. **3 piercing damage!** 

**Bramble: 9 → 6 HP** 💔

You grit your teeth. That's gonna leave a mark — and probably need washing. Twice.

---

### 🥊 Pip — Turn 1

The grin vanishes. Pip is *through* the door in a blur of bare feet and calloused knuckles, closing on the rat gnawing your arm.

**"Get OFF him!"**

Shortsword strike at Rat 1 (Drak is within 5 ft — wait, Drak isn't in yet. Pip is the first ally in though, so no Sneak Attack help for anyone yet). Pip attacks:
Pip shortsword — 1d20+5: 14 + 5 = 19
Pip damage — 1d6+3: 6 + 3 = 9

**9 damage!** Pip's blade flashes once, precise as a surgeon's cut, and the giant rat crumples with a wet squeak. The cheerful halfling cook just *one-shot* a dog-sized rat without breaking stride. 💀

**Rat 1: DEAD** ☠️

Pip flicks the blood from his blade and the grin is already creeping back. **"Nasty little thing. Bet it'd taste awful, too."**

Bonus action — unarmed strike at Rat 2 if it's within reach. It's about 10 feet away behind another crate — just out of range. Pip holds position next to you instead.

---

### 🧙 Eldon — Turn 1

From the doorway, Eldon points a finger — a tiny brass nozzle strapped to his index finger glows orange-hot.

**"Oh dear, oh dear — FIRE IN THE HOLE, as it were —"**

Fire Bolt at Rat 2:
Eldon Fire Bolt — 1d20+5: 12 + 5 = 17
Eldon Fire Bolt dmg — 1d10: 3 = 3

A bolt of flame sputters from the brass nozzle and streaks across the antechamber, singeing the second rat's flank. It squeals and whips around, fur smoking. **3 fire damage!**

**Rat 2: 7 → 4 HP** 🔥🐀

**"HA! Direct hit! The nozzle alignment is working — I adjusted the calibration this morning with a 3-degree —"**

**"ELDON."** That's Drak. One word. Enough.

---

### 🏹 Drak — Turn 1

Drak steps into the doorway, draws, and releases in one fluid motion. No wasted movement. No wasted breath. 🏹

Longbow at Rat 2:
Drak longbow — 1d20+5: 1 + 5 = 6

### 💀 Natural 1! Auto-miss!

The arrow *thunks* into a crate two feet above the rat's head. Drak stares at the miss. His jaw tightens. Talon makes a sound that might — *might* — be a derisive chirp. 🦅

**"...Wind,"** Drak mutters.

You're *inside a cave*, Drak.

---

### 🐀 Rat 2 — Turn 1

The singed, panicking rat bolts forward, lunging at the nearest target — that's Pip, standing right next to you!
Rat 2 bite Pip — 1d20+4: 2 + 4 = 6

**6 vs AC 15 — miss!** Pip sidesteps the lunge with a dancer's grace, the rat's teeth snapping on empty air. 💨

---

### 🗡️ BRAMBLE — YOUR TURN!

The second rat is right in front of you, smoking and furious, having just whiffed on Pip. Pip is standing within 5 feet of it — which means you've got an ally adjacent to your target.

You know what that means. 😈

**Sneak Attack is active!** You can add 1d6 to your damage if you hit.

You've got a dagger in hand and murder in your eyes. What do you do?

- 🗡️ **Stab it** — melee dagger attack with Sneak Attack
- 🗡️🗡️ **Stab it AND throw your second dagger** — attack + bonus action off-hand throw
- Something else?

**Bramble: 6/9 HP** | Rat 2: 4/7 HP 🐀🔥
That's what I'll do, stab and throw

Let's go, double dagger action! 🗡️🗡️

**Dagger attack on Rat 2** — Pip is adjacent, so Sneak Attack applies! (+5 to hit)
Bramble dagger — 1d20+5: 2 + 5 = 7

**7 vs AC 12 — miss!** 😬

Your dagger swipes through the air where the rat *was* a second ago as it flinches from its missed lunge at Pip. The blade catches nothing but smoke and singed rat hair.

**"Come HERE, you —"**

Bonus action: **Off-hand dagger throw!** (No Sneak Attack on this one — you can only Sneak Attack once per turn, and the off-hand throw doesn't add DEX to damage.)
Bramble dagger throw — 1d20+5: 19 + 5 = 24

**24 vs AC 12 — SMASH hit!** 🎯

You rip your second dagger free and hurl it sidearm in one furious motion. It spins once, catches the torchlight, and —
Bramble throw dmg — 1d4: 2 = 2

**2 damage!** The dagger buries itself in the rat's haunches. It squeals, stumbling — hurt, but still kicking. 🐀

**Rat 2: 4 → 2 HP**

---

### 👻 Vaelith — Turn 1

Vaelith steps to the doorway, obsidian pendant flickering at her throat. She extends one hand, fingers splayed dramatically.

**"Ugh. I just got these nails done."**

Eldritch Blast at Rat 2:
Vaelith Eldritch Blast — 1d20+5: 9 + 5 = 14
**14 vs AC 12 — hit!** A crackling beam of violet force lances from her palm — it sputters slightly, flickers, then *connects*. ✨
Eldritch Blast dmg — 1d10: 2 = 2

**2 force damage!** The beam hits the rat square in the chest and it tumbles backward, skids across the dusty stone floor, and goes still. 💀

**Rat 2: DEAD** ☠️

Vaelith examines her nails. **"Hmm. Barely worth the cantrip."** But you catch her flexing her casting hand behind her cloak — that sputtering flicker wasn't intentional. 👀

---

Mirael has been more relaxed than you've ever seen her. She walks with her hand trailing along bark, humming something elvish, occasionally stopping to examine a mushroom or listen to a birdsong. Without her staff, she's crafted a temporary focus from a twisted hazel branch, wound with wild ivy. It's not pretty, but it works. 🌿

Then you round a bend in the road and nearly trip over a man.

---

He's on his knees in the mud. Young — maybe twenty-five — with a shaved head, a logger's burly build, and a forearm wrapped in blood-soaked cloth. His eyes are wild, unfocused, the eyes of someone who's been running for hours and hasn't stopped being afraid.

**"Please —"** he gasps, grabbing at the nearest leg, which happens to be Drak's. Drak does not enjoy being grabbed. **"Please, you have to help — the wolves — they're not — they're not** ***natural*** **—"**

His name is **Bran**. The words tumble out in a panicked flood:

*The wolves came at the logging camp like soldiers. Surrounded them from three sides. Moved in formation. Destroyed every saw, every axe, every cart — but didn't kill anyone. It was a* ***message.*** *And every night, they hit the village. Closer. Bolder. The eyes — green eyes, glowing, all moving together like one animal in a dozen bodies.*

He's shaking. The bite on his arm is deep and angry-looking. Mirael is already kneeling beside him, pressing herbs to the wound without being asked. Her expression has changed — the relaxation is gone. Something in this story has her attention. 🌿👀

As Bran speaks, a sound rises from the treeline to the south. A howl — long, low, and beautiful. Then a second, from the east. Then a third, from the north. Three howls forming a **chord** — harmonizing in a way that no natural wolf pack has ever managed. 🐺🐺🐺

The hair on the back of your neck stands up.

Drak's hand finds his longbow. Talon screams from overhead and banks hard, gaining altitude. **"...Not natural,"** Drak confirms quietly. **"Three positions. Coordinated. They're watching us."** 🦅

Vaelith's pendant flickers at her throat. **"Oh, wonderful. Sentient wolves. Just what my week was missing."** But her eyes are scanning the treeline, sharp and alert. ✨

Pip puts a hand on Bran's shoulder. **"Easy now, friend. You're safe. How far to Thornfield?"** 🍞

**"Half a day,"** Bran croaks. **"Maybe less if you run. But I wouldn't — I wouldn't go through the forest after dark."** He swallows. **"They own the dark."**

Eldon adjusts his goggles, peering at the treeline. **"Coordinated pack behavior, luminescent ocular phenomena, tactical formation discipline... this has magical compulsion written all over it. Someone is** ***controlling*** **those wolves."** 🧙‍♂️
